title: Flat DVR special fibres are effective Cartier divisors
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and let $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Then the canonical inclusion of the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] at the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an effective Cartier centre: its kernel is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. The special fibre may be empty.

source.place: Tag 0EYJ, first paragraph; Tag 02OO, case (6) (flat pullback of an effective Cartier divisor)

proof.text: Choose an irreducible uniformizer pi using IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_irreducible. Its principal ideal is the maximal ideal by irreducible_iff_uniformizer, and pi is a nonzerodivisor in the domain A.

The residue-field inclusion is a closed immersion. Its kernel is the vanishing ideal of the closed point. On the top affine chart, use the Gamma-Spec isomorphism to identify this ideal with the comap of the maximal ideal. Regular principality is preserved by that ring isomorphism, so the kernel ideal sheaf is invertible.

The special fibre is the pullback along q of this residue-field inclusion. ker_fst_of_isClosedImmersion identifies its kernel with the comap of the invertible ideal. IsInvertible.comap_of_flat preserves invertibility; isEffectiveCartierCenter_iff_isInvertible_ker gives the conclusion.
